The statement conveys a credibly accommodative stance that is broadly supportive for growth. In New Keynesian terms (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), the explicit commitment to keep rates at the effective lower bound until inflation moderately exceeds 2% leverages expectations to stimulate current demand (consistent with Woodford’s expectations-centric framework). The continued large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS and supportive market operations align with the Bernanke–Gertler credit channel, easing financial frictions and maintaining accommodative financial conditions. At the same time, the nod to “substantial further progress” and monitoring of inflation expectations echoes Taylor rule–type reaction functions, and Orphanides’ caution about real-time slack measurement and lingering pandemic risks tempers exuberance. Net effect: cautiously optimistic with pro-growth policy support and anchored expectations, warranting a moderately positive sentiment above neutral but short of strongly positive.
